holder-quote: Navine’s awkwardness was plain. Probably over Xesci. Indeed, Brilm, Tasilt—Zail had had a number of words when he’d found out. But no one ‘knew’ anything.
“My class is [Courtesan of Change], more or less. High-level. Each time, I become someone either I or my client has met. It affects my personality too, so please excuse me.”
“You are not an agent of any power, or controlled by an influence besides your own, Xesci. Is that true?”

Xesci, the [Courtesan of Change], was the kind of person who had all the answers by her very nature. She did not—usually—give them out since there was such a thing as confidentiality and client privilege, especially in her line of work. These circumstances dictated otherwise.
Ishkr had long suspected that if Xesci wanted, the [Courtesan of Change] could transform to be anyone
She was a [Courtesan of Change], and she claimed she had forgotten her original face and form.
The [Courtesan of Change] had a weak class in that she was no [Wall Lord] or [General]
The truth was that [Courtesan of Change] was her old class. Her current one was a bit different.
The [Courtesan of Change] had forgotten that when she observed, the [Innkeeper] noticed.
Xesci heard out the vaguely convoluted string of events and sat there, cross-legged.
And then Osthia understood, because Xesci replied.
